commitResults.messageBody:
Replace the raw String task list with a Task class so each task
tracks its own description and done state, enabling mark/unmark.

Dispatch commands via a switch on the first word instead of
if/else "contains" checks.

Validate the task number before indexing into the list
(parseTaskIndex), so an out-of-range, non-numeric, or missing
argument prints a message instead of crashing.

Extract printWrapped/handleList/handleMark/handleAdd helpers to
remove the duplicated LINE-wrapping and mark/unmark logic that
is repeated across branches.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add ToDo, Deadline, and Event task types
commitResults.messageBody:
Introduce ToDo, Deadline, and Event as Task subclasses, each with
its own toString() format, and dispatch todo/deadline/event commands to handlers
that parse the command argument into the fields each type needs.

Deadline and Event arguments are split on their /by, /from,
and /to markers via indexOf rather than String.split(), since
that makes it straightforward to detect a missing marker (index
-1) and reject the command with a usage message instead of
constructing a task with a blank date/time. The default switch
case, which previously added any unrecognized command as a plain
Task, is replaced by the same style of usage-error message.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add test-ui skill for verifying console output
commitResults.messageBody:
Add a skill that runs test/ui-test-plan.md's test cases against the
compiled Steph program: each test case's commands are piped into one
program session, and the response after each command is checked
against the recorded expected output.

Comparing raw console output by hand doesn't scale past a couple of
commands and is easy to eyeball-pass on a subtly wrong string. The
runner script (scripts/run_ui_tests.py) does exact comparison instead,
splitting captured stdout into per-command blocks using the program's
own delimiter line so no test-specific parsing logic has to track
Steph's output format separately.

A `record` mode runs commands for real and prints ready-to-paste
Command/Expected-output blocks, so expected output always comes from
an actual run rather than being hand-typed -- a hand-typed block just
encodes a guess, and guesses that are wrong make a test lie in
whichever direction the mistake points

On a mismatch the runner stops immediately rather than continuing
through the rest of the test case or later cases, since a test case's
commands share state (e.g. `mark 1` depends on the `todo` before it),
so continuing past a wrong output would just cascade into more
failures that don't add information.

Seed the plan with six cases covering todo/deadline/event creation,
mark/unmark, and the two existing error paths (missing `/by`, unknown
command), each captured from a real run rather than typed by hand.

commitResults.messageTitle: Require test-ui after every source change
commitResults.messageBody:
Add a Testing section to AGENTS.md instructing that after any change
under src/main/java, test/ui-test-plan.md is updated if the change
affects console output, and the test-ui skill is run to confirm the
plan still passes.

Without this written down, a future session (or a future me) could
easily ship a change to command parsing or output formatting without
re-running the plan, since nothing else in the workflow forces it. The
section also says not to edit the plan to match broken output just to
make it pass -- a failure should be investigated (regression vs. stale
expectation) rather than silenced.

commitResults.messageTitle: Refactor error handing in Steph.java to use exceptions
commitResults.messageBody:
Add StephException (a checked exception carrying a user-facing
message) and have handleMark, handleAddToDo, handleAddDeadline, and
handleAddEvent throw it instead of calling printWrapped(...); return;
on invalid input. The unknown-command case in main's switch now
throws it too, instead of printing directly. A single try/catch
around the switch in main is the only place that calls printWrapped
for these errors.

Add a "delete <task-number>" command that removes the task at that
1-based position and reports the new task count, reusing the same
parseTaskIndex validation.

Add two test cases to test/ui-test-plan.md: one deleting a task and
confirming the remaining tasks renumber correctly in a following
list, and one confirming an out-of-range delete is rejected with the
same message style as the other commands' validation errors.

commitResults.messageTitle: Replace String command dispatch with a Command enum
commitResults.messageBody:
Add Command, an enum of the seven keywords Steph recognizes
(list/mark/unmark/todo/deadline/event/delete), each carrying its
exact keyword text. Steph.main now looks up the keyword via
Command.fromKeyword(...) and switches on the resulting enum instead
of switching on the raw String.
